### 📓 Docs Drift Check
⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/field-scale.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/field-scale.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fdb26698f975511a01a01f53d506058977db7cef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bf7b0ff033aa2a1d15fad07a0d29df9a79b6b367`

<sub>Read: card #19628 body, triage 5782023392, ruling 5791809146 (items 1–4), PM claim 5856375966, dev report 5856798203 (the PM's corrected id); PR #20248 object, body, file list, labels, 39 check-runs and the ruleset's required contexts on the head; the full diff against merge-base c02fa12767eeee8ffde3ff7e48830c182df2118f; `field-scale.ts`, `field-scale.test.ts`, `field.zod.ts` (`FieldSchema.useGrouping` TSDoc and describe), `package.json` files/exports, `tsup.config.ts`, `scripts/tsup-drop-sources-content.mjs`, the changeset gate headers, the `Check Changeset` job definition and its step outcomes, AGENTS.md's citation and changeset rules, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`'s published criterion, and objectui `packages/core/src/utils/number-display.ts` at the pinned `.objectui-sha` f8a9d0fb0596f4521076628e2bbfe27e6ce67d52. Ran: a TypeScript-scanner (6.0.2; repo pins 6.0.3) comments-stripped token diff of both files base vs head with a code-token positive control and a comment-only control; an assertion-sequence diff of the test; a byte cmp of the currency bullet; a tsc declaration-emit probe of base and head `field-scale.ts` with `resolveFieldScale`'s TSDoc as positive control; `git grep` over every checked-in `files[]` path at the head. NOT MEASURED: no local test execution (the shared checkout has no `node_modules` and no dev worktree is present in this container; CI's Test Core shards are the record), no local tsup build (the tsup `.d.ts` bundle and JS bundles are inferred from the tsc emit, esbuild's documented comment dropping and `sourcesContent: false`, not from a built dist), and no gate family was re-run locally.</sub>

### ① Derived judgments

(a) **No code token moves — holds.** `field-scale.ts` base c02fa1276 vs head bf7b0ff03 through `ts.createScanner` with trivia skipped: 123 = 123 tokens, `identical=true`, token-stream sha256 prefix `65aed4895c596175` on both sides (matches the dev's figure independently). Positive control (head with `percent: 0` changed to `percent: 1`): `identical=false`, first diff at token #20 `0` vs `1`, exit 1. Comment-only control (one docblock word changed): `identical=true`, while `cmp` reports the bytes differ, so the scanner is blind to comments and sensitive to code, as required. At the head there is no `number:` row (grep for a `number|currency|slider|rating` key row exits 1), `ABSENT_SCALE_BY_TYPE` still holds `percent: 0` only, and `resolveFieldScale`'s body is token-identical.

(b) **The test keeps its meaning — holds.** The 25 `expect(...)` statements, with line numbers stripped, are byte-identical in sequence between base and head (`diff` exit 0). `expect(resolveFieldScale({ type: 'number' })).toBeUndefined()` is still asserted (head :54) and `expect(resolveFieldScale({ type: 'currency' })).toBeUndefined()` is unchanged (head :61). With the `it` titles neutralised, the comments-stripped token diff of the test file is exactly one insertion at token #219: `}); it('T', () => {` between those two assertions, i.e. the split of one case into two and nothing else. The two-direction roster pin (`number: undefined` in the numeric-family map) is untouched. Test count goes 13 to 14 cases in the file by the split; no assertion added, removed or altered.

(c) **The docblock states the ruling faithfully — holds.** Head :59–:62 gives item 1 as the platform's declared answer: "an absent `scale` on a `number` field means NO fixed width — the value's natural precision — and that is the platform's declared answer, ⛔ not an open question (maintainer ruling 5791809146, batch 215 item 2, letter A′, 「215 同意」)". The citation is the ruling record's id, the same form the file already uses for 5749111840, 5791803339 and 5805782503; no tracker number stands as the citation (the only `#` references in the file are the pre-existing #19629 and objectui#9568/#10221, plus objectui#9843, which the ruling itself names as the carrier of items 2–3, used here as the carrier link, not as the citation). Items 2–3 are attributed to objectui#9843 at :66–:71 (footer and widget drop their private `?? 0` and read through `resolveFieldScale`; computed results round to the widest decimal count among the inputs, never a constant). Grouping at :71–:76 matches item 4: `FieldSchema.useGrouping` decides, the interim heuristic for an absent `useGrouping` reads the DECLARED `scale` only, never a resolved width, so nothing here moves a thousands separator. The stale sentence is gone: base :84 "`number` still awaits its own ruling" is replaced by head :95–:97 "`number`'s absent value is ruled to be no fixed width"; a grep for `awaits|nobody has ruled|not yet ruled|unruled|still open` at the head returns only the "not an open question" negation. The `currency` bullet (15 lines) is byte-identical base vs head (`cmp` exit 0). The batch-194 refusal is restated in the ruling's own words and its record is cited at :16. The `resolveFieldScale` TSDoc (unchanged) already says `undefined` means "no fixed width, the value's natural precision", and `FieldSchema.scale`'s describe says "omitted on any OTHER numeric type declares NO fixed width", so the three surfaces agree.

(d) **`skip-changeset` — holds; the docblock does not ship.** `@objectstack/spec` `files[]` is `dist, json-schema, liveness, prompts, llms.txt, README.md, src/**/*.zod.ts, CHANGELOG.md, api-surface, spec-changes.json`. `packages/spec/src/data/field-scale.ts` does not match `src/**/*.zod.ts`, so no source ships. `dist` types: tsc declaration emit of the file (base and head alike) carries only the declaration-attached TSDoc of `FieldScaleMeta` and `resolveFieldScale` (positive control "Callers must not spell a fallback" hits 1 in both) and 0 hits for the detached module docblock in either version ("What an ABSENT", "Why the table has exactly one row", "5791809146", "ruled to be no fixed width", "awaits its own ruling" all 0); `ABSENT_SCALE_BY_TYPE` is not exported and does not appear. tsup's `dts: { only: true }` pass bundles TypeScript's own declaration output, which cannot add comment text the emitter never produced. `dist` JS: esbuild drops non-legal comments (the docblock carries no `/*!`, `@license` or `@preserve`), and `tsup.config.ts` :35 states the same for this build. Source maps: `esbuildOptions: dropSourcesContent` sets `sourcesContent: false` (pinned by `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`). The checked-in published paths at the head give 0 hits for every docblock sentence; `api-surface/data.json`'s one `resolveFieldScale` hit is the signature entry `"resolveFieldScale (function)"`, no doc text. `json-schema` is generated from Zod describes, not from this file. Under AGENTS.md §3 (`skip-changeset` is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package) and os-dev.md :298 (published = what `files[]` actually ships), the label is correct and no `patch` changeset is owed. The PR diff carries no `.changeset/*.md` (added in ce8d3d398, removed in bf7b0ff03; net zero against the merge base).

(e) **The out-of-scope note — consistent with the truth, and non-blocking here.** At the pinned objectui sha f8a9d0fb, `number-display.ts:166–:172` is `shouldGroupDisplayNumber(scale?, currency?)`: money always groups, otherwise `return scale !== 0` with the in-line comment "Only an explicitly declared scale of 0 is an ordinal. `undefined !== 0`"; `formatDisplayNumber` :213–:215 sets `useGrouping = false` only when that returns false. No `min`/`max`/bound is read (dark control `zzzNotAFunction`: 0 hits). This PR's docblock ("a declared `scale: 0` marks a discrete integer and renders ungrouped; reads the DECLARED `scale` only") matches that reading and ruling item 4. The `FieldSchema.useGrouping` TSDoc in `field.zod.ts` :1262–:1265 ("`scale: 0` + no upper bound reads as a plain count and keeps grouping, a small bounded integer range reads as ordinal-shaped") does not match the pin: that is comment drift in an untouched file; the author-facing `.describe()` on :1285 says only "renderer decides (interim heuristic today, locale default eventually)", which is accurate. It is outside this PR's ruled file surface (item 1 names `field-scale.ts` only), the PR body records it in Acceptance notes, and nothing in this PR restates the bounds-based version, so it does not block. `field-scale.test.ts` :40–:42 ("a DECLARED 0 ... rendered ungrouped") is unchanged base text and is true of the interim heuristic.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` is declared on the PR body's second line and is right: no key, schema, export, signature or runtime behaviour moves (judgment (a)), and no published artefact of `@objectstack/spec` changes content (judgment (d)). No changeset is introduced, so `check-changeset-no-major`'s launch-window guard is vacuous and its level axis (a `yes` declaration must grade some package `minor` or above) is not engaged by a `no`. `check-empty-changeset`'s two rules (no empty-frontmatter changeset added; no foreign changeset modified) are not engaged by a diff that touches no `.changeset/*.md`. Level: none published; `skip-changeset` stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

Blocking: none.
Non-blocking: (1) the `FieldSchema.useGrouping` TSDoc drift in `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` :1262–:1265 (bounds-based description vs the pin's `scale !== 0`), noted by the dev with no carrier; a docs-only follow-up when someone next touches that block. (2) The `Check Changeset` `success` on this head was reached through the label exemption: step 9 "Settle the skip-changeset window" ran and steps 10–15 (require a changeset, etc.) were skipped, because `skip-changeset` was written at 14:36:17Z, 39 seconds after that run started; the `labeled` re-run at 14:36:21Z is `skipped` at job level by the fast path. That is the workflow's designed behaviour, and the exemption is justified by (d), but the green is the label's, not a measurement of publication. (3) GitHub had not yet computed `mergeable` (`unknown`) at both reads; the head is 3 commits on top of merge-base c02fa1276 with `main` at fdb26698f, and the two touched files are not touched by any other open PR per the PM claim's census (not re-taken here).

CI at this head: 39 check-runs, all `completed`; 31 `success`, 8 `skipped` (Auto Label, Check PR Size, Check Changeset on the `labeled` re-run, Packed-tarball smoke ×2 opt-in, Console Pin Gate, Build Docs), 0 failure/cancelled/timed_out/action_required. Every context the `main` ruleset requires is `success`: TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (and shards 1–6/6), Dogfood Regression Gate (and 1–3/3), Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard. Also `success`: Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Check Changeset (synchronize run), the four claim/closing-keyword guards, and the Vercel commit status. Closing keywords: the body carries exactly one, `Fixes #19628`; the only other `#` reference is `objectstack-ai/objectui#9843` in prose, not a closing keyword. Head unchanged across the review: `bf7b0ff033aa2a1d15fad07a0d29df9a79b6b367` on the PR object and on `refs/heads/claude/issue-19628-number-absent-scale-ruled` at the final re-read.
